Get started with wdauto

Source: vignettes/wdauto.Rmd
wdauto.Rmd

中文

wdauto keeps a local WebDriver service running on Windows so that R code, such as tidypptsdd, can drive Chrome or Edge. It needs x86 or x64 Windows, R 4.1 or newer, and the browser you want to use.

Browser Address Runs
Chrome, backend = "chromedriver" 127.0.0.1:4444/wd/hub ChromeDriver, no Java needed
Chrome, backend = "selenium" (default) 127.0.0.1:4444/wd/hub Selenium Server 3.141.59 on Java, for RSelenium
Edge 127.0.0.1:4445 Microsoft Edge WebDriver

Install 

install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("tony2015116/wdauto")
library(wdauto)

Start Chrome

Choose a folder for the drivers. get_cd() downloads the ChromeDriver that matches the installed Chrome, and auto_cs() starts the service and waits until it accepts connections.

driver_dir <- "C:/webdriver"

get_cd(driver_dir)
auto_cs(driver_dir, backend = "chromedriver")

Calling auto_cs() again reuses the running service. Clients that still use RSelenium and the legacy JSON Wire protocol need the Selenium backend, which also needs Java on PATH:

get_cd(driver_dir)
get_ss(driver_dir)
auto_cs(driver_dir)

Start Edge 

get_cd(driver_dir, browser = "edge")
auto_cs(driver_dir, browser = "edge")

Edge runs as a separate service with its own startup entry, so Chrome and Edge can run at the same time.

Download behind a slow or blocked network

Downloads try a mirror first and fall back to the official servers. In mainland China, set the mirror before the first download:

options(wdauto.mirror = "npmmirror")   # or Sys.setenv(WDAUTO_MIRROR = "npmmirror")
get_cd(driver_dir)

Other mirrors are given as URL prefix replacements:

options(wdauto.mirror = c(
  "https://storage.googleapis.com/chrome-for-testing-public" = "https://my.mirror/cft"
))

Without any network access, install archives that were downloaded on another computer:

get_cd(driver_dir, zip = "chromedriver-win64.zip")
get_ss(driver_dir, jar = "selenium-server-standalone-3.141.59.jar")

A cached driver for the same browser milestone is reused without network access, so the service can start offline after the first download.

Start at login and survive browser updates

By default auto_cs() writes a hidden startup entry for the current Windows account (wdauto_chrome.vbs or wdauto_edge.vbs in the Startup folder). At login it resolves the driver again and retries for about two minutes while the network comes up. The mirror option in effect when the entry was written is reused. Use autostart = FALSE for a one-time start.

When Chrome or Edge updates, the next auto_cs() call restarts the service with a matching driver if no browser session is open. Use restart = "never" to get an error instead.

Stop and troubleshoot 

reset_cs()                  # Chrome
reset_cs(browser = "edge")  # Edge

reset_cs() stops the managed service and removes its startup entry, even when the process record is damaged.

Problem Check
Port 4444 or 4445 is in use Another WebDriver, often an old Selenium started before upgrading, is running. Stop it, then call auto_cs() again.
The service does not start at login %LOCALAPPDATA%/wdauto/startup.log (Chrome) or %LOCALAPPDATA%/wdauto/edge/startup.log (Edge).
The driver fails during a session The service logs in %LOCALAPPDATA%/wdauto/webdriver-*/; the five newest are kept.
Downloads fail Set options(wdauto.mirror = "npmmirror"), or install an archive with zip =.
